title: Uniform asymptotic Fourier weight bound
statement: For every $\varepsilon>0$, there is a right-hand neighborhood of $0$ such that, for every $\alpha$ in that neighborhood with $\alpha\le1$, every natural number $n$, every function $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $0$ and $1$ whose uniform mean is $\alpha$, and every natural number $k\le(373/1000)\log(1/\alpha)$, the sum of the squared Fourier coefficients of $f$ over subsets of at most $k$ coordinates is at most $\varepsilon\alpha$.
hypotheses_covered: $\alpha$ lies eventually in the right-hand neighborhood of $0$
$f$ is a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube
